sentences.text: "Heard Sri Arvind Kumar Verma, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Diwakar Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on record.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of applicant Apil Verma, under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, with a prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 777 of 2022 for offence punishable under Sections 170, 389, 419, 420 of Indian Penal Code registered at Police Station- Kotwali Sadar, District- Kheri till the conclusion of trial, after rejecting the anticipatory bail application of the applicant by the Additional Session Judge, IIIrd, Kheri vide order dated 10.08.2022.

As per allegations made in the First Information Report dated 08.07.2022 15:48 hours which has been lodged by the first informant against the two persons, namely,
Mohit and Sumit on 08.09.2022 stating therein that the first informant received information on phone by Siraj while he was busy in the performing his duty that two persons came to his house and they introduced themselves as official of Crime Branch and they told him that he has a stolen mobile phone, if he did not give, he would have to pay fine and would be sent to Jail.
On the said information, police personnel reached the house of Siraj, where, two persons were already present.
They were arrested and they disclosed their names of Mohit and Sumit.
On query, they stated the name of the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
It is further submitted that in the F.I.R., no specific role or involvement has been attributed to the applicant.
It is further submitted that the name of the applicant has come into light in the statement of the co-accused Mohit and Sumit.
It is further submitted that the applicant is no more required for custodial interrogation.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedent to his credit.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready to participate in the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the applicant.
It is settled position of law that the anticipatory bail being an extraordinary privilege should be granted only in exceptional cases.

Parameters for grant of anticipatory bail in a serious offence are required to be satisfied, where the Court is prima facie of the view that the applicant has falsely roped in the crime and would not misuse his liberty.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98, ground for grant of ad interim anticipatory bail is made out.

On due consideration to the submissions advanced, perusal of the record so also the fact that charge-sheet in the matter has been filed, applicant has no criminal history, he has cooperated in the investigation and he shall cooperate in the trial, the interim protection granted by this Court vide order dated 31.08.2022 is made absolute in view of dictum of Apex Court in re: Sushila Aggarwal Vs.
State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98.
In view of the above, since, charge-sheet in the matter has been filed, the accused applicant-Apil Verma is directed to surrender before trial court, if he is summoned to face trial for offence in question.
